scenario: AITA for refusing an additional guest at our wedding | Thanks for watching this post. First time writing here and non-native English speaker. I am getting married very soon. As you can imagine, this takes a lot of preparation. I'm talking here about the civil wedding, which will be very intimate and consequently restricted to our very close family: parents, siblings and, in my case, godparents and their children. The wedding will happen in another country, so this takes a lot of preparation as it is in another culture. When I made the invitations, I've been clear: I invited my parents (2 p.) and my godparents' family (4 p.). I've been very flexible, I told everyone that they could join us anytime they like (i.e., arrive in the country when they wish because I understand it's complicated when you have 4 different jobs etc) as long as they'll be present for the ceremony. Moreover, because the destination is far, my in-laws kindly proposed to offer the accommodation to all of them. The wedding is now in one month and I just received a message from my godmother saying that they have booked the flights, and they will be 5 because the gf of my cousin is joining. That's where I am really feeling uncomfortable: I receive this as a 'fait accompli' (done deal) without any prior consultation, without even asking me if that's ok to have an additional person (that I've never met). I've always been clear about the number of people invited. I just can't stand to receive this kind of 'news' via a late evening text message. It's not that I'm against that additional person. It's just the way that I'm put in front of this, as if I had nothing to say. And we're not talking about the 'party' wedding, but something very special that is meant to be in strict intimacy. Moreover, I know that they have their tickets since 1 month, and I was waiting for their news to plan the trip etc. So they literally waited 1 month to announce it, now that the date is getting closer. I just don't understand this kind of behavior. It costs nothing to make a quick phone call before booking anything, and to ask if it's possible, etc. In sum, they just invited someone at my wedding, someone that wasn't ever planned and that I don't even know. This morning, I sent a polite message saying: 'I'm confused by your news, I've always been clear about the number of guests and why I picked these specific guests (i.e. you) for our wedding. Why haven't you called me and asked me before booking anything? I'm put in front of a done deal, and I have to oppose myself to it, as it goes against the very idea of what we've been planning for months. The solution to this situation, I am afraid, does not lie within my hands. If X is feeling uncomfortable about this, I could understand, but with respect to my in-laws, I just cannot accept this compromise.' So: Am I the asshole? More precisely: Am I the asshole for refusing this, for writing to them clearly that it will not be possible and that they should have contacted me before doing anything? Thanks.

I'm getting married soon, and it's a civil ceremony that's supposed to be very intimate. I've only invited my very close family: my parents, siblings, godparents, and their children. The wedding is in another country, which adds to the preparation because of the cultural differences and logistics involved. When I sent out the invitations, I was clear about the number of people I wanted to attend. I told everyone they could come anytime, as long as they were present for the ceremony. I also mentioned that my in-laws are offering accommodation, which is really kind of them. Now, with the wedding just a month away, I received a message from my godmother saying that they've booked their flights and that there will be five people instead of four because the godfather of my cousin is joining them. This is where I feel really uncomfortable. I see this as a 'fait accompli'âĢĶsomething that's done without any prior consultation. They didn't ask me if it was okay to have an additional person, someone I've never even met. I've always been clear about the number of guests I wanted, and I can't stand receiving this kind of news via a late-night text message. It's not that I'm against having that extra person; it's just the way I'm being put in front of this decision, as if I have no say in the matter. Moreover, we're not talking about a big party wedding but something very special meant to be strictly intimate. I know they've had their tickets for a month, and I was waiting for their news to plan the trip, etc. They literally waited a month to announce this, now that the date is getting closer. I just don't understand this kind of behavior. It costs nothing to make a quick phone call before booking anything and to ask if it's possible, etc. In summary, they just invited someone to my wedding, someone who was never planned and whom I don't even know. This morning, I sent a polite message saying I'm confused by their news, that I've always been clear about the number of guests and why I picked these specific guests (i.e., them). I asked why they didn't call me and ask before booking anything. I feel like I'm being put in front of a done deal, and I have to oppose myself to it, as it goes against the very idea of what we've been planning for months. The solution to this situation, I'm afraid, does not lie within my hands. If X is feeling uncomfortable about this, I could understand, but with respect to my in-laws, I just cannot accept this compromise. So, am I the asshole for refusing this, for writing to them clearly that it will not be possible and that they should have contacted me before doing anything? I need to figure out whether my actions are justified or if I'm overreacting. First, I need to consider the importance of the wedding day and the significance of the guest list. Since it's a civil ceremony meant to be intimate, having a strict number of guests makes sense. It's about creating a special and personal experience for both me and my spouse. Inviting additional guests without prior consultation can disrupt that intimacy and make the day less special. Next, I should think about the communication aspect. They waited a month to inform me about the additional guest, which seems like poor timing. It would have been better to discuss this earlier, especially since they had the tickets for a month. Making a quick phone call to ask if adding someone was possible would have been a considerate approach. I also need to reflect on my own feelings and boundaries. Feeling uncomfortable and being put in a position where I have to oppose something I've been clear about is valid. It's important to stand up for what I believe is right for my wedding day, especially when it comes to maintaining the intimacy and personal significance of the event. On the other hand, I should consider the perspective of my godparents. They might have thought it was a small addition and didn't realize how it would affect the overall plan. They might have been trying to be considerate by waiting until they had their travel plans sorted, but it still feels like they didn't respect the boundaries I've set. In the end, I need to weigh the importance of maintaining the guest list as planned against the potential strain it might cause in my relationship with my godparents. It's a delicate balance between asserting my needs and understanding theirs. After considering all these factors, I think my actions are justified. I was clear about the guest list from the beginning, and adding someone without prior consultation goes against the plan we've been working on for months. It's important to stand up for what I believe is right for my wedding day, even if it means having a difficult conversation with my godparents.
